newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle 1996 sales seen up around seven pct.
newsitem.headline: Nestle 1996 sales seen up around seven pct.

text.p: Financial analysts said they expected Nestle SA to announce tomorrow that group sales rose around seven percent in 1996, boosted by the weakening Swiss franc and volume growth as well.
"We expect growth of seven percent from 56.5 billion Swiss francs ($39.9 billion) to 60.6 billion," Credit Suisse First Boston said in an research report.
"The Swiss franc's weakening in November and December 1996 had a positive currency influence on both sales and net profit."
It forecast 10 percent growth in the last two months of 1996, making for a 2.1 percent currency boost for all of 1996.
"We see EPS rising 9.2 percent from 74.4 Swiss francs in 1995 to 81.2 francs. If current exchange rates hold in 1997, sales could grow 16 percent in 1997."
It said sales likely grew around 2.8 percent by volume last year, down from stronger rates in early 1996 that were triggered primarily by comparisons with weak coffee prices in early 1995.

Union Bank of Switzerland saw sales up 7.2 percent to 60.55 billion. It attributed 3.0 percentage points to volume growth, 2.3 points to currency factors, 1.3 points to price increases and 0.6 percent to acquisitions.

Volume sales growth in eastern Europe remains strong at around 30 percent, but was around 2 percent in western Europe. Sales were flat in France, Nestle's biggest European market, but German sales rose around 3.0 percent, it said.
SBC Warburg was at the lower end of forecasts, seeing sales up around 5.9 percent in 1996. An analyst who asked not to be identified said the difference reflected currency assumptions.

"It is all about currency, clearly. I think some players are factoring an average 1.25 (dollar/franc exchange) rate for 1996. We have an average rate of around 1.22. That is mainly the one percent that is missing there," the analyst said.

SBC Warburg also saw volume growth of three percent, below some of the more optimistic outlooks for 3.5 percent growth. Its other sales components were 1.4 percent pricing, 0.7 percent acquisitions and 0.8 percent currency factors.

"As for currencies, it starts to get very interesting for Nestle in 1997," he said, noting SBC Warburg raised its 1997 EPS forecast by five percent to 91 francs and adjusted its share price target to 1,550 from 1,480 primarily for currency factors.
Almost half of Nestle's sales are posted in dollars.
Nestle chairman Helmut Maucher said in November it expected around 60 billion francs in 1996 sales. Sales were up 5.7 percent to 48.3 billion in the first 10 months of the year.
-- Michael Shields, Zurich newsroom +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.414 Swiss Francs)
